 Frequently asked questions about KRA’s tax amnesty as deadline nears
 Monday 09th November, 2026 04:23 PM | 
 By David Nthua 
 A Tax amnesty poster. 
 The Kenya Revenue Authority (KRA) offers a 100 per cent waiver on qualifying penalties, interest and fines under its 2026 Tax Amnesty Programme.
 The programme began on July 1, covering qualifying debts accrued by December 31, 2025. On Monday, November 9, 2026, KRA’s official FAQs still listed December 31 as the deadline; People Daily had reported on the authority’s reminder .
 KRA defines tax amnesty as “the pardon and vacation of accrued interest, penalties and fines upon meeting certain given conditions.”
 Who qualifies?
 KRA says taxpayers with no principal tax outstanding but with qualifying penalties, interest or fines qualify automatically. Those with unpaid principal tax must settle it in full by December 31, 2026, to receive the waiver.
 A section of KRA office. PHOTO/@KRACorporate/X 
 Must taxpayers apply? 
 No application is needed where principal tax was already cleared. KRA says iTax automatically waives eligible penalties and interest. Those with outstanding principal tax can pay at once or seek a payment arrangement through iTax, as explained in this People Daily guide to the amnesty .
 What if returns were not filed? 
 Taxpayers with missing returns for periods up to December 31, 2025, can qualify by filing them. Those with nil returns and no principal tax due qualify for waiver of late-filing penalties after filing outstanding returns. Where tax is due, full payment is required.
 Other tax amnesty rules
 Are 2026 debts included? 
 No. KRA says liabilities and related penalties and interest arising from January 1, 2026, are excluded and remain payable. Customs duties under the East African Community Customs Management Act are outside the programme.
 Can disputed debts qualify? 
 Yes. Taxpayers with cases in court or before the Tax Appeals Tribunal are advised to use Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) to agree on principal tax and settle it within the programme period.
 How is the waiver confirmed? 
 Once conditions are met, an amnesty certificate is sent to the taxpayer’s iTax-registered email. It is also available through Consult and Reprint in iTax.
 Taxpayers must clear outstanding principal tax under payment plans by December 31, 2026. KRA advises taxpayers to review ledgers and resolve missing payments, return amendments and disputes before the deadline.
